name: Zero Resource Speech Challenge 2020
description: We present the Zero Resource Speech Challenge 2020, which aims at learning speech representations from raw audio signals without any labels. It combines the data sets and metrics from two previous benchmarks (2017 and 2019) and features two tasks which tap into two levels of speech representation. The first task is to discover low bit-rate subword representations that optimize the quality of speech synthesis; the second one is to discover word-like units from unsegmented raw speech. We present the results of the twenty submitted models and discuss the implications of the main findings for unsupervised speech learning.
evaluation_method: ABX error (subword discriminability) and precision/recall/F1 for spoken-term discovery (word-like unit discovery)
general_score_metric: ABX error rate (primary for subword task)
reputation: Well-regarded research benchmark in unsupervised speech learning (builds on the 2017 and 2019 challenges) and widely used in the zero-resource/unsupervised speech community.
notes: Non-LLM audio benchmark with heterogeneous task-specific metrics (ABX and STD metrics). Designed for unsupervised representation learning from raw audio; not saturated and primarily used in research contexts.
